message.content:
Let  
\[
a=\log(2009)=\ln(2009).
\]
Since
\[
4036081=2009^2,
\]
we have
\[
\log(4036081)=\log(2009^2)=2\log(2009)=2a.
\]

Now use the identities
\[
\cos(ix)=\cosh x,\qquad \sin(ix)=i\sinh x.
\]
Thus
\[
\cos(ai)=\cosh a,
\]
and
\[
\sin(2ai)=i\sinh(2a).
\]
So the expression becomes
\[
2\cosh^2 a+i\cdot i\sinh(2a)
=2\cosh^2 a-\sinh(2a).
\]
Using identities,
\[
2\cosh^2 a=1+\cosh(2a),
\]
so
\[
2\cosh^2 a-\sinh(2a)
=1+\cosh(2a)-\sinh(2a).
\]
Since
\[
\cosh x-\sinh x=e^{-x},
\]
we get
\[
1+e^{-2a}=1+e^{-2\log(2009)}
=1+\frac{1}{2009^2}.
\]
Finally,
\[
2009^2=4036081,
\]
so the expression simplifies to
\[
1+\frac{1}{4036081}=\frac{4036082}{4036081}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{4036082}{4036081}}\).
